items.title: Workflow lab: Test ideas with code layers and the Figma agent

items.title: How Figma manages sandboxes at scale
items.summary: Figma’s AI products require tens of thousands of sandboxes to run untrusted code safely. That’s why we built Nimbus: a platform that makes sandboxes fast, reliable, and easy for Figma product teams and operators to manage.

items.title: How to put your design system to work with the Figma agent

items.title: How to lighten design system upkeep with the Figma agent

items.title: Single-shot and agentic retrieval with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports single-shot RAG and retrieval-only requests through AgenticRetrieveStream, alongside agentic retrieval. This post explains how the maxAgentIteration parameter matches retrieval effort to each request, using an illustrative internal banking policy assistant.

items.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Learn what’s new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with it on Amazon Bedrock.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter multimodal vision-language model, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. Deploy the NVFP4 or BF16 variant in a few steps, then run text, image, and video inference for document intelligence, computer-use agents, and multimodal agentic workloads.

items.title: Pluggable Agentic AI Framework: A seven-layer composable enterprise agentic AI reference architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: A seven-layer composable reference architecture for taking enterprise agentic AI from prototype to production on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each layer has a stable contract, so you can swap technologies at any layer without redesigning the rest of the stack.

items.title: How CrossnoKaye grounds physical AI with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: CrossnoKaye brought physical AI to heavy industry with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Its ATLAS platform and AURA agentic system ground AI reasoning in live plant data and run verifiable Python in isolated AgentCore sandboxes, giving plant engineers checkable, math-backed answers instead of model guesses.

items.title: Professional work deserves professional tools. Meet AWS Quick.
items.summary: Introducing AWS Quick, formerly Amazon Quick, and the debut of our first brand campaign celebrating teams who keep business moving. AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work, where teams use AI agents to research, analyze, and act across the data and applications they already rely on.

items.title: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker Inference now supports GPU partitioning with NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which divides one GPU into hardware-isolated partitions so you can run a different model in each or take a right-sized fraction of a newer accelerator. This post shows how two optional API fields place one model per partition, and what we measured against a whole older GPU.

items.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in AWS Quick
items.summary: As we built Amazon Quick, its agents grew from answering questions to taking actions, and the same primitives kept getting rebuilt under different names. This post shares the taxonomy we converged on — triggers, agents, capabilities, and learned context — found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When, What, Who, and How.

items.title: Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate
items.summary: Learn how to build a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate that gives AI agents secure, metadata-driven access to an enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON file, with no per-dataset integration code.

items.title: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 2
items.summary: In Part 1 you built one governed agent. Part 2 scales the pattern to an enterprise: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes the single front door and redeems Okta’s grant, Cedar policies bind each tool to the agent, a second agent runs on Amazon EKS, and AgentCore Observability traces every allow and deny beside Okta’s log in Amazon CloudWatch.
